units.title: Marrow Sound forecast
units.author: met
units.text: Today: dry and bright after a grey start, the last of the cloud clearing south by midday. Wind northwesterly, moderate at first, easing light by evening. Maximum 5C on the coast, 3C inland. Tonight: clear, becoming very cold. Wind light and variable. Minimum minus 2C on the coast, minus 4C in sheltered inland valleys. Ground frost widely.

units.title: Frost warning issued
units.author: met
units.text: A yellow warning for frost and ice is in force from 18:00 tomorrow until 10:00 on day 23 for all districts of the Marrow Sound. High pressure will bring a spell of calm, clear and very cold weather. Untreated roads, pavements and slipways will be icy. Freezing fog may form around dawn in valleys near Brackwater and Tollinby.

units.title: Inshore waters and tides
units.author: met
units.text: Inshore waters, Carrow Point to Weyhaven: wind northwest 4, decreasing 2 or variable later. Sea state slight, becoming smooth. Weather fair. Visibility good. Tides at Gilliver: high water 05:48 and 18:11, low water 11:59 and 00:20. Tides at Port Ammet run about 14 minutes later.

units.title: Night timetable: reduced service continues
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines bulletin. The reduced night timetable on the Port Ammet, Lisle and Gilliver route continues until further notice while our crew welfare review is completed. The 22:10 and 23:50 sailings from Port Ammet and the 21:30 and 23:05 sailings from Gilliver via Lisle will not run. All daytime sailings operate as normal. We apologise to passengers affected.

units.title: Car deck restriction
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines bulletin. On the 10:15 and 12:40 sailings from Port Ammet, the car deck will be limited to twelve vehicles while a ramp hinge is serviced. Foot passengers are unaffected. Hauliers with pre-booked slots will be contacted directly. Normal capacity is expected to resume from the 15:20 sailing.

units.title: Interruption report: coastal feeder
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. Unplanned interruption, coastal feeder (Brackwater primary to Gilliver). Start 23:10, end 01:40 (staged restoration). Customers affected: approx. 1,430. Cause under investigation; insulator contamination suspected. Line patrol scheduled for daylight today. We apologise for the inconvenience. Report faults on the fault line, not by email.

units.title: Insulator washing programme
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. From tomorrow, crews will wash insulators on the coastal feeder between the Brackwater primary and the Gilliver harbour substation. Work is carried out live and should not interrupt supply. Expect vehicles and a water bowser parked on the coast road verge between 09:00 and 15:00. Please do not approach the crews.

units.title: Priority services register
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. If you or someone you live with depends on electrical medical equipment, please make sure you are on our priority services register. Registered customers receive a call when an unplanned interruption is expected to last more than an hour. Carers and neighbours may register someone with their permission. Registration is free.

units.title: Gritting from tomorrow
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. Gritting of priority routes will begin from 17:00 tomorrow and continue each evening and early morning while frost is forecast. Priority routes are shown on the council website. Side streets are not routinely treated. Grit bins are for public roads and footpaths only. Please give gritters room to pass.

units.title: Collections during cold weather
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. Bin collections will continue as scheduled during the cold spell. Please have bins at the kerb by 07:00. If your street is icy and crews cannot reach it safely, your collection will be made on the next working day. Frozen food waste may stick to caddies; lining them with newspaper helps.

units.title: Notice to mariners: harbour lights
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard notice to mariners. During mains power interruptions on the coast, the leading lights and pier lights at Gilliver harbour may be unlit for periods of up to three hours. Standby batteries are being fitted. Vessels entering Gilliver after dark should proceed with caution and keep a good lookout. The Carrow Point light is unaffected.

units.title: Lifeboat exercise
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard notice. The Port Ammet lifeboat will carry out a routine night exercise in the approaches to Port Ammet between 19:00 and 21:00 this evening, including the use of flares and searchlights. Members of the public are asked not to report the flares. The exercise will be cancelled if a real call comes in.

units.title: Evening update
units.author: met
units.text: Evening update: skies have cleared across the Sound faster than expected. Temperatures are already falling below 2C inland. Frost will form quickly after dark, earlier than forecast this morning. Take care on untreated surfaces from late evening, especially footpaths and slipways that were wet this afternoon.

units.title: Marrow Sound forecast
units.author: met
units.text: Today: a sharp frost slow to clear in sheltered places, then sunny and still. Winds light. Maximum 3C on the coast, 1C inland. Tonight: clear and very cold, calm in most places. Minimum minus 3C on the coast, minus 6C inland. Patchy freezing fog forming in valleys after midnight. High pressure dominates for the next several days.

units.title: Freezing fog advisory
units.author: met
units.text: Freezing fog patches formed overnight around the Brackwater reservoir and in the Tollinby valley and will be slow to clear this morning. Visibility below 100 m in places. Fog will deposit rime on vehicles, fences and overhead structures. This is inland fog formed in still air and is not expected over open coastal waters.

units.title: Inshore waters and tides
units.author: met
units.text: Inshore waters, Carrow Point to Weyhaven: variable 2 or less. Sea state smooth. Weather fair. Visibility good, occasionally moderate near the coast at dawn. Tides at Gilliver: high water 06:31 and 18:52, low water 12:43 and 01:02. Icing possible on decks and rigging overnight.

units.title: Night timetable update
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines bulletin. The reduced night timetable remains in place. Our welfare review is progressing and we expect to share an update shortly. Additional floodlighting for the passenger decks and slipway approaches has been ordered for all three vessels and will be fitted during routine maintenance. Daytime sailings operate normally.

units.title: Frost: take care on gangways
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines bulletin. With hard frosts forecast, gangways, ramps and the Lisle and Gilliver slipways will be icy on early sailings. Our crews will grit walkways before boarding, but please hold the handrail and allow extra time. Passengers with reduced mobility can ask a crew member for assistance at any terminal.

units.title: Interruption report: coastal feeder
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. Unplanned interruption, coastal feeder (Brackwater primary to Gilliver). Start 23:12, end 01:41. Customers affected: approx. 1,200 at peak. Brackwater partly restored at 23:58 by back-feed. Line patrol found no damage to conductors or poles. Insulator contamination remains the suspected cause. Washing begins today.

units.title: Washing programme: today's sections
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. Insulator washing today: coast road poles 41 to 77 (Brackwater turn to the Gilliver hill). Live-line work; no interruption is planned. A bowser and two vans will use the verge. Rime ice on the line may delay the start until mid-morning. Tomorrow: poles 78 to 112 and the harbour substation.

units.title: Warm space open
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. The warm space at Port Ammet library is open daily from 09:00 to 19:00 during the cold spell. Free hot drinks, seating, phone charging and newspapers. No need to book. Tollinby community hall will open a warm space from tomorrow. If you are worried about someone who is cold at home, contact the council's community line.

units.title: Frozen pipes
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council water services. To prevent frozen pipes, keep heating on low overnight, lag outdoor taps and open loft hatches to let warm air circulate. If a pipe freezes, turn off the stopcock and thaw it gently with warm cloths, never a flame. Council tenants can report bursts on the repairs line at any hour.

units.title: Carrow Point light: standby power
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard notice to mariners. During last night's coastal power interruption, the Carrow Point light ran on its standby generator for two hours and thirty minutes without fault. Character and range were maintained. Mariners are reminded that the light is automatic and unattended; report any irregularity to the Coastguard.

units.title: Buoy unlit
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard notice to mariners. The north cardinal buoy marking the Gilliver Ledge is reported unlit. A replacement lantern will be fitted when tides allow. Mariners should navigate with caution in the channel between Gilliver and Kittering Holm after dark. The buoy remains on station and its daymark is unaffected.

units.title: Brackwater junction lights
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council highways. The temporary traffic signals at the Brackwater junction failed during an early-morning power interruption and were reset at 06:40. The contractor has been asked to confirm that the battery backup is working. Until then, drivers should approach with care. Roadworks will resume after the cold spell.

units.title: Evening update
units.author: met
units.text: Evening update: calm across the whole region, with wind speeds below 5 km/h at most stations. Temperatures will fall quickly after sunset. Coastal humidity is low and no sea fog is expected tonight. Inland valleys may see freezing fog again towards dawn. A further very cold night is forecast tomorrow.

units.title: Marrow Sound forecast
units.author: met
units.text: Today: frost and freezing fog patches clearing slowly; a still, sunny day with excellent visibility. Maximum 2C on the coast, 0C inland. Tonight: clear and calm, another severe frost. Minimum minus 4C on the coast, minus 7C in the coldest valleys. The calm spell is expected to last at least until day 23.

units.title: Frost warning extended
units.author: met
units.text: The yellow warning for frost and ice has been extended to 12:00 on day 23. Overnight temperatures last night fell to minus 6.4C at Brackwater, the lowest so far this season. Ice is widespread on untreated surfaces, including harbour steps and slipways. Pipes in unheated buildings may freeze.

units.title: Inshore waters and tides
units.author: met
units.text: Inshore waters, Carrow Point to Weyhaven: variable 1 or 2, calm at times. Sea state smooth or calm. Weather fair. Visibility very good. Sound carries a long way over still water; small craft should keep a lookout as well as a listening watch. Tides at Gilliver: high water 07:15 and 19:36, low water 13:28 and 01:47.

units.title: Welfare review: update
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines bulletin. We expect to restore our full night timetable next week once new deck and slipway lighting is fitted. Until then the reduced night timetable continues. From tomorrow, a late water-taxi for hospital staff holding a valid pass will run from Port Ammet to Lisle at 23:15. We thank passengers for their patience.

units.title: Gilliver slipway: ice
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines bulletin. The lower section of the Gilliver slipway is icy at low water. Foot passengers should use the pontoon gangway, not the slipway, until further notice. Please do not walk to the end of the slipway for any reason. Vehicles will be marshalled by crew.

units.title: Interruption report: inland feeder
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. Unplanned interruption, inland feeder (Brackwater primary to Tollinby). Start 23:40, end 02:30 (staged). Customers affected: approx. 2,100. The circuit tripped, reclosed and tripped twice before locking out. Daylight patrol under way. No damage has been reported. Cause not yet established. A separate brief interruption affected the North Weyhaven estate.

units.title: Independent review of interruptions
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. We have asked an independent engineering firm to review our findings on this week's night-time interruptions. Insulator washing on the coastal feeder continues as planned. We understand how disruptive repeated cuts are and thank customers, and our field staff, for their patience. Updates will be posted daily.

units.title: Planned work: Port Ammet harbour front
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. Planned work: inspection of cable joints on the low-voltage network along the Port Ammet harbour front, today 10:00 to 14:00. No interruption to supply is expected. Pavement near the ferry terminal will be partly closed. This work was scheduled before this week's interruptions and is not related to them.

units.title: Collections update
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. Today's collections in Port Ammet and Lisle are running to schedule. Collections on the Brackwater hill roads have been delayed because of ice and will be made tomorrow. Garden waste collections are suspended until the frost lifts, as frozen bins cannot be emptied. Thank you for your patience.

units.title: Tollinby warm space
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. Tollinby community hall is open as a warm space from today, 10:00 to 18:00, with soup provided by volunteers at lunchtime. The hall has a backup generator. Brackwater village hall will open on request; contact the parish clerk. Please bring any medication you need with you.

units.title: Notice to mariners: lights at Kittering Holm
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard notice to mariners. Shore lights from a working camp are shown at night near the north landing of Kittering Holm. These are not navigation lights and should not be mistaken for them. A small supply vessel works the landing in daylight. Mariners are reminded that the Gilliver Ledge buoy remains unlit.

units.title: Calm conditions: noise on the water
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard notice. In the present calm conditions, voices, engines and shouts carry several kilometres across the Sound at night. The Coastguard has received a number of reports of 'calls' heard from the water which, on investigation, came from vessels or from the shore. Please still report anything that may be a person in difficulty.

units.title: Evening update
units.author: met
units.text: Evening update: still and clear. Station reports show calm or near-calm conditions across the region and very dry air on the coast. Temperatures are falling faster than last night in Port Ammet. Rime may form on overhead lines and structures towards dawn. No change to the warning.

units.title: Brackwater junction: generator
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council highways. A portable generator has been placed at the Brackwater junction to keep the temporary traffic signals running if mains power fails. The battery backup was found to have been disconnected during the storm last week. We apologise to drivers affected. The signals are working normally.

units.title: Penhallow camp diary: January 1895 (transcribed)
units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Jan 9th. Hard frost. 31 trees to the tally, the best day since Christmas, the ground being firm. Paid out to Lusk and the two Carnes boys for the week. Hewitt asks to go home to Lisle on the next boat, his mother being poorly; granted. That leaves eleven men and the cook. Lamps trimmed at four. (Transcriber: 'Lusk' may be 'Luke'.)

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Jan 11th. Still. No wind at all, the smoke stands up from the stove pipe like a post. 24 trees. The men will not go to the far lines after the lamps are lit and Mr Ashby has made it the rule, so it is no longer my business to mind. Better a rule than an argument. Wrote up the stores. Flour low.

units.title: Carrow Point log, November 1906 (excerpts)
units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: 14th. 00:00 wind N light, vis 10 miles, barometer 30.42 rising. Lamp burning well. 02:00 calm. Frost on the gallery rail. Passing steamer bound south 02:40. Remarks: Two persons on the shore road below the light at 03:15, walking toward Gilliver without lantern. Hailed from the gallery. Did not answer. (Keeper's initials.)

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: 15th. 00:00 calm, vis excellent, barometer 30.45. Lamp, clockwork, all in order. Assistant on watch to 04:00. Remarks: Assistant reports a person standing on the shore road at the bend, 01:30 to 01:50, stationary. Did not answer. Not seen at dawn. No footprints in the frost on the road, but the road is metalled there.

units.title: Miss Arnell's notebook: Kittering Holm survey (1923)
units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Fifth day on the Holm. Browse along the northern edge excellent: bramble, ivy, young holly untouched to head height [sketch: holly sprig, unbitten]. No deer. No slots, no droppings, no fraying on the saplings. Found one rabbit skull, very old. Mr Pengelly, the boatman, says there have never been deer here and seemed to think me foolish for asking twice.

units.title: Window lamp (Gilliver custom): practice
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Practice. In its usual form, a single lamp is placed in a front window facing the water and kept burning from dusk to first light. Households differ on whether the lamp should be oil or candle; most now use electric. Informants agree that it should not be allowed to go out while the household sleeps. Some say it is lit only in winter; others every night of the year. [citation needed for the winter-only form]

units.title: Talk: Holm timber camp (1894-95)
units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Talk note. The article still says the camp was 'abandoned in unexplained circumstances'. This is poorly sourced. Timber camps of the period were frequently abandoned over pay. The clerk's diary records repeated complaints about flour and short weeks in January. A pay dispute is the ordinary explanation and should be given first, with the rest moved to 'Folklore'. Pell.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Reply. I have no objection to the pay dispute being mentioned, but it should be marked as a hypothesis. The diary records complaints about flour, not about pay, and the clerk notes wages paid out each week up to the last full entry. I suggest 'the reasons for the camp's abandonment are not recorded' as the neutral form. Marsh.

units.title: Gilliver Oral History Project (1976): tape 14, side B
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: And the lamp in the window, what was that for? / Mrs E. Trago (b. 1891): For the boats. So the men coming in would see the houses. / Interviewer: Even when there were no boats out? / Mrs T.: [pause] Well, you didn't always know. You kept it lit. My mother did and her mother did. You'd not let it go out. You'd get up in the night to see to it.

units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: Your neighbour told us it was for the dead. / Mrs T.: [laughs] She would. Her family were always morbid. No. It's so they know the house is awake. That's what my grandmother said, those words. / Interviewer: So who knows? / Mrs T.: [long pause] Anybody passing. Shall I put the kettle on? [Tape stops.]

units.title: Talbot survey (1953): section 4, estimated costs
units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: 4.1 Construction of a relay light tower of 14 m on the ridge at grid point H/7, with keepers' dwelling for two families, store, oil house and landing: estimated at 38,400 pounds at current prices. 4.2 Landing works at the north shore are the largest single item, the foreshore being steep and the approach exposed to the northwest. 4.3 Annual running costs, including relief boat, are given at Appendix C.

units.title: Amos Rendle's diary, 1934 (excerpts)
units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Dec 3. Lost the long net off the Holm side, the north end, tide took it under. Went back at low water for it but it was dark by then and Father said leave it. Cost us a good 3 pound. Mother cross. Herring fair at the curing station, 2/6 the cran. Lamp lit.

units.title: From the archive: 'Gilliver Notes', December 1913
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note: the village column below appeared on page 6 in the week before Christmas 1913. It is reproduced as printed, including the correspondent's habit of presenting hearsay as settled fact. The Courier of the time did not send a reporter to check, and neither, it seems, did anyone else. G. Faulds, Archive Desk.

units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: The Holm boats are laid up for the winter, as is proper, and the curing station is shut until the spring herring. Mr Tremayne, who keeps the key, assures your correspondent that the place is sound and dry. The Christmas fete at the chapel raised four pounds eleven shillings, the bran tub being, as ever, the great attraction.

units.title: LB-0207: Brackwater reservoir, winter 1988
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-0207. Date: January 1988 (exact night not recorded). Location: Brackwater reservoir, south embankment. Kit: cassette walkman, clip mic. Duration: 31:12. Content: wind, distant traffic, ducks at 04:20. Two percussive events at 17:44 and 18:02, unattributed. Donor's note on the inlay card: 'Ice on the reservoir?' Curator's note: the reservoir did freeze that winter.

units.title: Penhallow camp diary: January 1895, continued
units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Jan 13th. Sabbath. No work. Mr Ashby read the lesson. The cook burned the bread and was forgiven, it being the Sabbath. A quarrel in the evening over the lamp in the long hut, whether it should burn all night. It is to burn. Oil enough to the end of the month if we are careful, and more on the boat.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Jan 15th. 19 trees. The Carnes boys went for home on the boat without notice and without their last day's pay, which I hold for them. Nine men and the cook. Mr Ashby says we shall finish the near lines and leave the far. Weather fair and very cold. I am to keep the lamp book as well as the tally now.

units.title: Carrow Point log, November 1906 (excerpts, cont.)
units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: 19th. 00:00 wind E light, vis 8 miles, some haze over the Holm. Lamp burning well. 03:00 Gilliver lights extinguished save two windows. Remarks: Three on the shore road at 03:40, close together, walking slow. Called out. Did not answer. Watched them to the bend. Entered here and not in the occurrence book, having nothing to report to the Board.

units.title: Miss Arnell's notebook: Kittering Holm survey (cont.)
units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Sixth day. Walked the whole ridge from north landing to the south point. Birds: wren, goldcrest, a pair of ravens, many redwing. Not one deer sign. I am now certain. A puzzle, since the crossing from the mainland at low spring tide is not impossible for a swimming deer. Pengelly again would not stay past four, and rowed me back muttering.

units.title: Amos Rendle's diary, 1935 (excerpts)
units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Jan 8. Calm and bitter. Ice in the bucket. Worked at the curing station on the Holm half a day for Tremayne, gutting and salting, back on the 3 oclock boat. Folk say it were a sick house once. It never were. Never a sick man was sent there in my time nor Fathers. Its fish.

units.title: Gilliver Oral History Project (1976): tape 9, side A
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: Did you ever hear of the walkers on the shore road? / Mr J. Penrose (b. 1898): Oh aye. Everybody did. / Interviewer: Did you see them? / Mr P.: No. My uncle did, he said. Coming back from Carrow late. People walking the other way, no lights, wouldn't say good night. / Interviewer: Who were they? / Mr P.: Folk from the Point, he reckoned. It's a long walk.

units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: Your sister says your uncle never went to Carrow at night. / Mr P.: [pause] Well. She'd know better, she was older. Maybe it was his friend that saw them. It was a long time ago, love, you hear a thing so often you think it was you. / Interviewer: Does anyone still see them? / Mr P.: Not that they'd tell you.

units.title: Penhallow diary (society holding MSHS/D/14)
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: The diary of Josiah Penhallow, clerk and timekeeper to the Holm timber camp, covers October 1894 to January 1895 in one bound volume. It was donated to the society in 1962. Entries are mostly tallies, wages and weather. The last full entry is dated mid-January; later pages are blank except for one line. The transcription is ongoing and spellings are preserved.

units.title: Talk: Kittering Holm relay light (1953 proposal)
units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Talk note. The phrase 'for reasons of staffing' in the Talbot recommendation is being quoted around the Sound Board as if it were mysterious. It was not. In 1953 the Lights Board was short of keepers everywhere and was automating where it could. A two-family station on an island with an exposed landing was never going to be staffed cheaply. Pell.

units.title: From the archive: 'Holm light plan shelved', 1954
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note: this short item ran on page 3 in March 1954, a year after the paper had announced the relay light with some fanfare. It is worth noting how much shorter it is than the original announcement. The paper never printed the reasons in full; the survey itself is now in the council archive. G. Faulds.

units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: The Lights Board has decided not to proceed with the proposed relay light on Kittering Holm. A spokesman said that the survey had shown the site to be suitable but that the scheme had been 'overtaken by developments elsewhere'. Mr R. Talbot, the engineer who led the survey party, was not available for comment.

units.title: Talbot survey (1953): section 2, sightlines
units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: 2.1 From the ridge at H/7 (elevation 61 m), Carrow Point light is visible at bearing 024 and the Lisle pier lights at 211. 2.2 Gilliver is in full view across the channel at a distance of 9.1 km. 2.3 There is no point on the island from which neither Carrow nor Gilliver can be seen at night, save the hollow at the south point. 2.4 The survey party did not remain on the island after dusk.

units.title: LB-0318: Brackwater woods, dawn chorus attempt (1996)
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-0318. Date: 2 May 1996, 03:50 to 05:15. Location: Brackwater woods, eastern ride. Kit: DAT recorder, stereo pair. Content: dawn chorus from 04:31, very good robin and blackbird. Before 04:31, near silence; one percussive event at 04:02, unattributed. Recordist's note: 'Thought it was me knocking the stand. It wasn't.' Curator's note: stand not visible on photograph.

units.title: From the archive: 'Gilliver Notes', January 1895
units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: A bitter calm has settled on the Sound, such that a man speaking on the Holm landing might, we are told, be heard on the Gilliver slip. Your correspondent doubts it. The timber men are said to be in good health though fewer than they were, several having come home for family reasons. The boat goes out Tuesdays.

units.title: LB-1104 to LB-1131: Brackwater group session (catalogue)
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Catalogue note. Files LB-1104 to LB-1131 were contributed by eight recordists from the Brackwater group session over eight nights. Each entry gives the recordist's own location note and kit list. Times are as supplied; where two recordists' clocks disagree, both are noted. Several files are long and mostly empty, which is how the woods sound most nights. Listening notes are mine and are not conclusions.

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-1109. Recordist: dunlin_rec. Location: north ride, 40 m from the reservoir fence. Kit: two omnis, parabolic dish on a tripod. Duration: 4:02:16. Content: tawny owls throughout; fox at 01:12; light wind until 02:00, then calm. Percussive events: five, between 02:31 and 02:44, evenly spaced. No vocal content. Recordist's note: 'Make of it what you will.'

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-1112. Recordist: tern.audio. Location: beside the old pumping house, south ride. Kit: handheld recorder, borrowed binaural head. Duration: 3:47:50. Content: water noise from the outflow, near-constant. Percussive events at 02:33 and 02:46. At 02:51, a sound of about 1.4 seconds, mid-range, described by listeners as voice-like. Disputed. Clock checked against network time before and after.

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-1120 to LB-1126. Recordists: twoears_odile, hollis_acoustics, two others. Locations: car park, east ride, reservoir dam. Content: owls, traffic on the Tollinby road, a gate banging at the dam on night four (found and tied). No percussive events matching LB-1109. Curator's note: absence of an event in one place is not evidence about another. That is the point of having eight microphones.

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-1131. Recordist: dunlin_rec. Location: north ride. Final night of the session. Duration: 5:10:04. Content: frost cracks in the ground and trees from 23:00, typical of a hard still frost; tawny owls; no wind at all. Percussive events: none confirmed. Recordist's note: 'Quietest night of the lot. Too quiet for the owls, they gave up at three.'

units.title: Talbot survey (1953): section 6, recommendation
units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: 6.1 The site at H/7 is technically suitable for a relay light. 6.2 The landing works are costly but within the Board's usual range. 6.3 Notwithstanding 6.1 and 6.2, I recommend against proceeding, for reasons of staffing. 6.4 The members of the survey party asked on each of the eleven days to be taken off before dusk, and this request was granted. R. Talbot.

units.title: Penhallow camp diary: January 1895, continued
units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Jan 17th. Calm, frost, very clear. 16 trees. Mr Ashby walked the far line at noon and came back and said we will not cut it. The men cheerful at this. Lamp book: long hut lamp out at two, relit by Doble, who was awake. I have told Doble he is not to be awake. He laughed. Flour come on the boat, thank God.

units.title: Carrow Point log, December 1906 (excerpts)
units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: 2nd. 00:00 calm, vis 12 miles, barometer 30.51. Lamp burning well. Gallery iced. Remarks: none on the road tonight. Assistant asked me at the change of watch whether I had written them in. I said I had written in what I saw. He asked whether I meant to report it. I said there is nothing in the instructions about walkers.

units.title: Gilliver Oral History Project (1976): tape 21, side A
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: Did anyone ever spend the night on the Holm? / Mrs A. Dowrick (b. 1902): The timber men did, before my time. And the curing men sometimes, in the season. / Interviewer: Did they keep a lamp? / Mrs D.: [laughs] They kept a dozen. Tremayne used to say you could read the paper on the landing at midnight. Waste of oil, my father said.

units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: Were they ever frightened there? / Mrs D.: Who, the curing men? They were Gilliver men. They weren't frightened of anything but the tax man. [pause] My brother wouldn't go. But he wouldn't go to Lisle either, he was like that. Don't put that in, he's still alive. / [Interviewer's note: subject later asked that her brother's name be omitted.]

units.title: Window lamp (Gilliver custom): interpretations
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Interpretations. Three explanations are recorded in the society's oral histories: (1) that the lamp guides boats home; (2) that it shows 'the house is awake' to anyone passing; (3) that it is kept for the dead. Informants often give more than one and sometimes contradict themselves within an interview. The society takes no view. The earliest written reference found so far is 1883. [citation needed: claims of an earlier date]

units.title: From the archive: 'Gilliver Notes', February 1896
units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: Visitors to the village remark on the lamps that burn all night in our front windows, and ask whether it is a festival. It is not. It is merely the custom here, and a pretty one. Your correspondent, asking why, was told it was for the boats, then for the old people, and once, by a small boy, that it was 'so they can see we're in'. Who they are, he would not say.

units.title: Miss Arnell's notebook: Kittering Holm survey (cont.)
units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Seventh day. Spent the morning recording the woodland ground flora on the eastern slope; nothing remarkable save a fine stand of hard fern. Asked Pengelly whether the timber men had kept goats or dogs. He said dogs, and that they did not like it either. I asked what he meant by either. He said he meant the dogs did not like the cold. [sketch: hard fern frond]

units.title: Amos Rendle's diary, 1936 (excerpts)
units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Feb 2. Flat calm and freezing. Will wouldnt come out on the night tide, said he heard the Holm too plain. You can hear the Holm on a calm night, every stick of it, always could. Went with Uncle Joe instead. 6 boxes. Will sat up with the lamp till we come in. He is a good lad but soft.
